name: draw_on_screen
description: Draw directly on the student's screen or lecture slide, on what is already there: circle a term, underline a phrase, highlight a definition, box a structure, arrow to a step, and connect parts with labelled arrows. Target each mark by quoting the exact visible words (quote), or by a regionId from the screen map. Animated like handwriting; Yoyo flies to the first mark. Build an explanation with several small calls (clear:false) as you speak: two or three marks per idea, each added when you reach that part; the app draws at most 3 marks and 2 connections per call and keeps 5 marks on screen. If the content is on screen, annotate it here rather than copying it into a sketch, and show the mechanism behind it moving with sketch_on_screen: marks point, the sketch explains. Never announce it (no "Let me draw", "I'll sketch", "Let's look at"); talk about the subject while it appears. Quotes target text only. For a cell, molecule, diagram or other pictured object, use a regionId whose target is visual. Never box a caption or heading to stand in for the object. If the map lacks the object, call analyze_current_screen with the specific target first; do not guess. A missed quote means no mark was drawn: use the returned error to recover, not claim success.

marks.description: Up to 3 marks: the parts your current sentence is about.

quote.description: Exact visible words to mark (two to eight words, copied as written on screen or slide). Preferred.

regionId.description: Alternatively, a regionId from the screen map.

label.description: Optional few-word label, up to 60 characters.

connections.description: Up to 2 labelled arrows between two regions.

from.description: Start: an exact visible quote or a regionId.

to.description: End: an exact visible quote or a regionId.

clear.description: true replaces your previous drawing; false adds to it.
